interest: NBC's 1934 Fourth of July broadcast with Japan.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.46/1 through 894.46/3) documents arrangements for an international Fourth of July radio broadcast exchange between the United States and Japan in 1934, organized by the National Broadcasting Company (NBC) in cooperation with the Japanese Broadcasting Company (JOAK). NBC initially requested that a State Department official speak during the American segment of the program alongside a scheduled Tokyo broadcast featuring Japanese Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota and U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew. State Department officials, including Special Assistant James Clement Dunn, Under Secretary William Phillips, and Far Eastern Affairs Chief Stanley K. Hornbeck, evaluated the proposal and advised that any American address strictly avoid political references to the sensitive 'Far Eastern situation' and focus purely on American history. The issue was resolved when NBC learned from Tokyo that Foreign Minister Hirota would not participate due to limited English proficiency and had been replaced by Prince Iesato Tokugawa in an unofficial capacity, leading NBC and the State Department to agree that unofficial American figures, such as Henry W. Taft or William R. Castle, should speak instead of government officials.
